targets.title: The Sybil Attack
targets.authors: John R. Douceur
targets.why_needed: States the identity-forgery problem and proves that without a logically centralized identity-issuing authority, no distributed protocol can bound the number of identities one entity presents, except under resource-parity and coordination assumptions the paper states as unrealistic. Every other target in this domain is a proposed way around, or a measurement of the limits of, this result.

targets.title: SybilGuard: Defending Against Sybil Attacks via Social Networks
targets.authors: Haifeng Yu, Michael Kaminsky, Phillip B. Gibbons, Abraham Flaxman
targets.why_needed: First social-graph Sybil defense: bounds accepted Sybil identities per attack edge by intersecting random routes, assuming the honest region of the graph is fast-mixing. Originates the whole random-walk/random-route social-graph defense family that SybilLimit, SybilRank, SybilInfer, Ostra, Bazaar, Canal, and Integro all descend from or are compared against.

targets.title: SybilLimit: A Near-Optimal Social Network Defense against Sybil Attacks
targets.authors: Haifeng Yu, Phillip B. Gibbons, Michael Kaminsky, Feng Xiao
targets.venue: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy
targets.why_needed: States a tightened bound on accepted Sybil identities per attack edge relative to SybilGuard (O(log n) versus O(sqrt(n log n))) under the same fast-mixing assumption; the number every later social-graph defense states its own improvement against. The IEEE/ACM Trans. Netw. 2010 journal version (doi 10.1109/TNET.2009.2034047) is the extended text.

targets.title: Aiding the Detection of Fake Accounts in Large Scale Social Online Services
targets.authors: Qiang Cao, Michael Sirivianos, Xiaowei Yang, Tiago Pregueiro
targets.why_needed: SybilRank: ranks accounts by the landing probability of short random walks from a trusted seed set rather than by pairwise random-route intersection; deployed at Tuenti (a production social network), giving a rare production-deployment measurement to compare against the purely simulated defenses.

targets.title: SybilInfer: Detecting Sybil Nodes using Social Networks
targets.authors: George Danezis, Prateek Mittal
targets.why_needed: Replaces the deterministic random-route intersection of SybilGuard/SybilLimit with Bayesian inference over the whole social graph, returning a probability that each node is a Sybil rather than a binary accept/reject; states its own false-positive/false-negative tradeoff curve to compare against the deterministic schemes.

targets.title: SybilBelief: A Semi-Supervised Learning Approach for Structure-Based Sybil Detection
targets.authors: Neil Zhenqiang Gong, Mario Frank, Prateek Mittal
targets.venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security
targets.why_needed: Applies loopy belief propagation to a graph seeded with a small labeled set of known-honest and known-Sybil nodes, generalizing SybilRank's single-class seed to two-class semi-supervised inference; states an accuracy comparison against SybilRank and SybilInfer on the same graphs.

targets.title: SybilSCAR: Sybil Detection in Online Social Networks via Local Rule Based Propagation
targets.authors: Binghui Wang, Le Zhang, Neil Zhenqiang Gong
targets.why_needed: States a unified local-rule propagation framework that it claims subsumes SybilRank, SybilBelief, and SybilFuse as special cases and gives a formal linear-approximation convergence guarantee that the earlier structure-only methods lack; the convergence proof is the specific thing to extract.

targets.title: SybilFuse: Combining Local Attributes with Global Structure to Perform Robust Sybil Detection
targets.authors: Peng Gao, Binghui Wang, Neil Zhenqiang Gong, Sanjeev R. Kulkarni, Kurt Thomas, Prateek Mittal
targets.venue: IEEE Conference on Communications and Network Security (CNS)
targets.why_needed: Combines per-node local classifier scores (account attributes) with global graph-propagation scores as a weighted-edge input to SybilBelief-style propagation, on a Tuenti dataset with two attackers evading detection differently; states a robustness comparison under structure-only attacks that pure graph methods do not survive.

targets.title: Ostra: Leveraging Trust to Thwart Unwanted Communication
targets.authors: Alan Mislove, Ansley Post, Peter Druschel, P. Krishna Gummadi
targets.why_needed: Applies the same attack-edge-limiting idea as SybilGuard to message-delivery credit rather than identity acceptance: a sender consumes and later refunds a link-capacity credit along the social-graph path to the recipient, bounding unwanted messages per attack edge without any global computation. A distinct application of the same underlying assumption, with its own deployment-scale measurement (a crawl of an online social network).

targets.title: Bazaar: Strengthening User Reputations in Online Marketplaces
targets.authors: Ansley Post, Vijit Shah, Alan Mislove
targets.why_needed: Applies the Ostra link-credit mechanism to marketplace transaction reputation instead of message delivery, computing a per-transaction risk score from network flow along the trust graph; evaluated on a crawl of a real online marketplace with measured fraud outcomes, giving comparison numbers for flow-based reputation against pure rating-count schemes.

targets.title: Canal: Scaling Social Network-Based Sybil Tolerance Schemes
targets.authors: Bimal Viswanath, Mainack Mondal, P. Krishna Gummadi, Alan Mislove, Ansley Post
targets.why_needed: States that the per-query graph traversal cost of SybilGuard-family and Ostra/Bazaar-family schemes prevents deployment on graphs at real social-network scale, and gives a landmark-routing precomputation that answers the same queries approximately at far lower cost; carries the specific accuracy-versus-cost tradeoff numbers for approximate social-graph defenses.

targets.title: Íntegro: Leveraging Victim Prediction for Robust Fake Account Detection in OSNs
targets.authors: Yazan Boshmaf, Dionysios Logothetis, Georgos Siganos, Jorge Lería, José Lorenzo, Matei Ripeanu, Konstantin Beznosov
targets.why_needed: States that fake accounts preferentially befriend a predictable subset of honest users ("victims") and that down-weighting edges to predicted victims before running SybilRank-style propagation raises detection robustness against an adversary who forms attack edges strategically rather than at random, the specific adversary construction Viswanath (SIGCOMM 2010) and Alvisi (S&P 2013) showed defeats prior schemes. The Computer & Security 2016 journal version (doi 10.1016/j.cose.2016.05.005) is the extended text with a Tuenti production deployment.

targets.title: Whanau: A Sybil-proof Distributed Hash Table
targets.authors: Chris Lesniewski-Laas, M. Frans Kaashoek
targets.why_needed: Builds routing tables directly from the social graph via random-walk sampling so that lookup correctness depends only on the count of attack edges, not on the count of Sybil identities, tolerating O(n/log n) attack edges with O(sqrt(n) log n) state per node and constant-round lookups; the one target system in this domain that is itself a DHT rather than a classifier layered on one, giving a direct alternative to Kademlia-family routing under adversarial identity creation.

targets.title: A Sybil-proof One-hop DHT
targets.authors: Chris Lesniewski-Laas
targets.why_needed: Precursor construction to Whanau: routes lookups through a small set of social-graph-sampled introducers in a single hop rather than Whanau's multi-hop layered routing table; states the earlier, simpler version of the sampling argument Whanau's proof builds on.

targets.title: An Analysis of Social Network-Based Sybil Defenses
targets.authors: Bimal Viswanath, Ansley Post, P. Krishna Gummadi, Alan Mislove
targets.why_needed: Shows by direct simulation on four real social-graph datasets that SybilGuard, SybilLimit, SybilInfer, and a simple community-detection baseline all in fact perform local community detection around the trusted seed, that a graph whose honest region is itself partitioned into distinct communities is therefore more vulnerable regardless of which of these four schemes is used, and that an adversary who chooses which honest nodes to attach to (rather than attaching uniformly at random) is measurably more effective — the specific finding every later social-graph defense (Canal, Integro, SybilFuse) must be checked against.

targets.title: SoK: The Evolution of Sybil Defense via Social Networks
targets.authors: Lorenzo Alvisi, Allen Clement, Alessandro Epasto, Silvio Lattanzi, Alessandro Panconesi
targets.venue: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy
targets.why_needed: Unifies SybilGuard, SybilLimit, SybilRank, SybilInfer, and GateKeeper under one local-community-detection framework, states that the choice of community-detection subroutine changes detection accuracy substantially even holding the surrounding scheme fixed, and states that a simple degree/feature classifier already matches graph-based methods against a random-attachment adversary while no published method as of 2013 was sufficient against a targeted-attachment adversary — the exact gap the brief's open problem 3 asks whether anything since has closed. The 2014 Internet Mathematics journal version (doi 10.1080/15427951.2013.865685, "Communities, Random Walks, and Social Sybil Defense") is the extended text.

targets.title: Measuring the Mixing Time of Social Graphs
targets.authors: Abedelaziz Mohaisen, Aaram Yun, Yongdae Kim
targets.why_needed: Directly measures the mixing time of real social graphs (Facebook, LiveJournal, and others) rather than assuming it; every social-graph Sybil defense's stated bound holds only for a fast-mixing honest region, so this is the primary-source check on whether that precondition holds in deployed graphs. Cited by both Viswanath (SIGCOMM 2010) and Alvisi (S&P 2013) as the source of the mixing-time concern each critique raises.

targets.title: Uncovering Social Network Sybils in the Wild
targets.authors: Zhi Yang, Christo Wilson, Xiao Wang, Tingting Gao, Ben Y. Zhao, Yafei Dai
targets.why_needed: Ground-truth measurement of Sybil accounts banned by a real deployed social network operator (Renren), giving observed attack-edge counts, attachment strategy, and behavioral signatures from an actual adversary population rather than a simulated one — the comparison point for every synthetic-attacker evaluation among the targets above. The 2014 ACM TKDD journal version (doi 10.1145/2556609) is the extended text.

targets.title: SybilDefender: Defend Against Sybil Attacks in Large Social Networks
targets.authors: Wei Wei, Fengyuan Xu, Chiu C. Tan, Qun Li
targets.why_needed: Uses short random walks from a single suspect node (rather than from a trusted seed set) to decide whether that node is a Sybil, and separately clusters detected Sybils into communities to remove them in bulk; states its own scalability numbers (walk length, node count) as a specific alternative to SybilRank's global-ranking approach.

targets.title: Sybil-Resilient Online Content Voting
targets.authors: Dinh Nguyen Tran, Bonan Min, Jinyang Li, Lakshminarayanan Subramanian
targets.why_needed: SumUp: bounds the count of votes an adversary's Sybils can cast on a piece of content by max-flow capacity along the social graph from voters to a trusted set of vote collectors, adaptively throttling links whose flow saturates; a max-flow-based construction contemporaneous with and structurally distinct from the SybilGuard random-route family, applied to a content-voting rather than identity-admission problem.

targets.title: The Eigentrust Algorithm for Reputation Management in P2P Networks
targets.authors: Sepandar D. Kamvar, Mario T. Schlosser, Hector Garcia-Molina
targets.why_needed: Computes each participant's single global trust score as the principal left eigenvector of the matrix of normalized pairwise ratings, requiring a pre-trusted seed set to guarantee convergence; the foundational global-reputation construction every later peer-to-peer reputation system (PowerTrust, HonestPeer, EERP) states its comparison against, and the concrete case of the seed-set centralization problem the brief's domain description flags.

targets.title: PowerTrust: A Robust and Scalable Reputation System for Trusted Peer-to-Peer Computing
targets.authors: Runfang Zhou, Kai Hwang
targets.venue: IEEE Transactions on Parallel and Distributed Systems
targets.why_needed: Exploits a measured power-law distribution in peer feedback frequency to select the most-rated peers as distributed random-walk seeds instead of a fixed pre-trusted set, stating a specific convergence-speed and accuracy comparison against EigenTrust on the same simulated eBay-derived rating distribution.

targets.title: PeerTrust: Supporting Reputation-Based Trust for Peer-to-Peer Electronic Communities
targets.authors: Li Xiong, Ling Liu
targets.venue: IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering
targets.why_needed: Computes trust from three measured components (feedback received, total transaction count, feedback-source credibility) plus two context-adaptive weights, rather than a single eigenvector score; states its own simulation results on a P2P transaction model comparing against EigenTrust and a no-trust baseline, giving the multi-factor alternative's specific cost and accuracy numbers.

targets.title: Attack-Resistant Trust Metrics for Public Key Certification
targets.authors: Raph Levien, Alexander Aiken
targets.why_needed: Originates the max-flow formulation of trust propagation later refined into the Advogato metric: trust flows from a seed set through a certification graph and each edge carries a capacity bounding how much trust it passes, so a single adversary-controlled identity is bounded by the capacity of its incoming edges rather than by network size. Levien's 2009 book chapter "Attack-Resistant Trust Metrics" (doi 10.1007/978-1-84800-356-9_5) is the direct Advogato-specific description; this 1998 paper is where the max-flow construction and its bound are proved.

targets.title: Propagation Models for Trust and Distrust in Social Networks
targets.authors: Cai-Nicolas Ziegler, Georg Lausen
targets.why_needed: Appleseed: computes local group trust by injecting energy at a source node and spreading it along outgoing trust edges by a tunable spreading-factor parameter, rather than by max-flow; states its own accuracy comparison against Advogato's max-flow metric on the same trust graph, giving the energy-spreading alternative's specific tradeoff against the flow-capacity bound.

targets.title: The Beta Reputation System
targets.authors: Roslan Ismail, Audun Jøsang
targets.why_needed: Models the expected probability of a good outcome from one participant as (positive ratings + 1) / (positive + negative ratings + 2), a beta-distribution posterior updated in constant time per rating with no global computation; the elementary bilateral-rating building block that later multi-factor systems (PeerTrust) and marketplace systems (Bazaar) combine with a graph-level mechanism rather than using alone.

targets.title: Combating Web Spam with TrustRank
targets.authors: Zoltán Gyöngyi, Hector Garcia-Molina, Jan O. Pedersen
targets.why_needed: Biased PageRank walk seeded from a small manually-verified trusted page set, propagating trust along hyperlinks with attenuation per hop; designed for web spam rather than peer reputation, later adapted to peer-to-peer settings, so it states a distinct trust-seeding mechanism (manual verification of a small seed) to compare against EigenTrust's and PowerTrust's automatic seed selection.

targets.title: HonestPeer: An Enhanced EigenTrust Algorithm for Reputation Management in P2P Systems
targets.authors: Heba A. Kurdi
targets.venue: Journal of King Saud University - Computer and Information Sciences
targets.why_needed: States a modification to EigenTrust that redistributes query load away from the fixed pre-trusted seed set (the concentration effect the brief's domain description flags), reporting simulation numbers against unmodified EigenTrust on the same peer population; the specific claim to check is whether the redistribution still requires a seed set or removes the dependency entirely.

targets.title: EERP: An Enhanced EigenTrust Algorithm for Reputation Management in Peer-to-Peer Networks
targets.authors: Alanoud Alhussain, Heba A. Kurdi
targets.why_needed: A second, later modification to EigenTrust's seed-concentration problem by an overlapping author with HonestPeer; states its own comparison against both unmodified EigenTrust and HonestPeer, which is the specific number needed to determine whether either enhancement actually removes the seed-set dependency or only reduces its measured effect.

targets.title: TrustGuard: Countering Vulnerabilities in Reputation Management for Decentralized Overlay Networks
targets.authors: Mudhakar Srivatsa, Li Xiong, Ling Liu
targets.why_needed: States and measures strategic-oscillation (a peer alternating good and bad behavior to stay above a reputation threshold) and collusion (peers rating each other falsely high) as concrete attacks on transaction-based reputation systems, with a specific decay-weighted and collusion-detection countermeasure and its measured effect on attacker gain; the primary source for the collusion and self-promotion attack categories the domain brief lists.

targets.title: The Social Cost of Cheap Pseudonyms
targets.authors: Eric Friedman, Paul Resnick
targets.why_needed: Formal game-theoretic proof that when a low-reputation identity can be costlessly discarded and replaced (whitewashing), every equilibrium must either penalize newcomers relative to established identities or accept a lower level of cooperation than a costly-identity system achieves; the primary source for the whitewashing attack category and the specific reason identity-creation cost enters the design at all.

targets.title: A Survey of Attack and Defense Techniques for Reputation Systems
targets.authors: Kevin Hoffman, David Zage, Cristina Nita-Rotaru
targets.why_needed: Decomposes published reputation systems into a common set of components (rating, aggregation, storage, punishment) and classifies attacks by which component they target, giving a structured taxonomy of self-promotion, slandering, whitewashing, and identity-multiplication (Sybil) attacks against reputation specifically, each cited to its originating system; the single most exhaustive attack-classification source named in this domain.

targets.title: Computational Puzzles as Sybil Defenses
targets.authors: Nikita Borisov
targets.venue: IEEE International Conference on Peer-to-Peer Computing (P2P)
targets.why_needed: States the core difficulty in using proof-of-work against Sybil creation — a solved puzzle must not be reusable, or an attacker solves once and replays the solution for every identity — and gives a decentralized all-to-all challenge-broadcast construction whose combining function proves each solution incorporated a fresh challenge from every other participant; the foundational forgery-cost construction for the proof-of-work sub-family named in the domain brief.

targets.title: Resource Burning for Permissionless Systems
targets.authors: Diksha Gupta, Jared Saia, Maxwell Young
targets.why_needed: Generalizes proof-of-work into "resource burning" — any mechanism that forces an entity to provably waste a scarce, unforgeable resource (computation, bandwidth, storage, or time) as the price of an identity or an action — and surveys the design space and known bounds across resource types, not only computation; states which resource choices admit provable Sybil-resistance bounds and which remain open, directly relevant to whether a non-computational resource can substitute for a trusted seed identity.

targets.title: Interpreting Graph-Based Sybil Detection Methods as Low-Pass Filtering
targets.authors: Satoshi Furutani, Toshiki Shibahara, Mitsuaki Akiyama, Masaki Aida
targets.venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security
targets.why_needed: Recasts SybilRank, SybilBelief, and related propagation-based detectors as instances of graph signal low-pass filtering, and uses that unification to state a shared structural limitation — the filtering view exposes exactly which graph-frequency components each method is blind to — providing a theoretical rather than empirical critique that applies across the whole propagation-based family at once, including the newer GNN-based detectors.

targets.title: Enhancing Sybil Detection via Social-Activity Networks: A Random Walk Approach
targets.authors: Xiaoying Zhang, Hong Xie, Pei Yi, John C. S. Lui
targets.venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing
targets.why_needed: Extends random-walk Sybil detection from the pure social graph to a joint social-activity network (edges from both social links and behavioral co-activity), stating that activity edges carry detection signal social structure alone does not, with its own measured detection-accuracy comparison against structure-only random-walk methods (SybilRank, SybilWalk) on the same datasets.

targets.title: TrustGCN: Enabling Graph Convolutional Network for Robust Sybil Detection in OSNs
targets.authors: Yue Sun, Zhi Yang, Yafei Dai
targets.why_needed: Applies a graph convolutional network, trained on node features plus structure rather than structure-only propagation rules, to Sybil detection, stating a measured accuracy comparison against SybilRank and SybilBelief on the same graph; one of the earliest graph-neural-network Sybil detectors and the direct predecessor the domain brief's request for 2023-2026 GNN work is measured against.

targets.title: Attacking Graph-Based Classification without Changing Existing Connections
targets.authors: Xuening Xu, Xiaojiang Du, Qiang Zeng
targets.why_needed: States an evasion attack against graph-based classifiers (the family SybilRank, SybilBelief, and GNN-based detectors all belong to) that adds only new attacker-controlled nodes and edges among them, never modifying or removing any existing honest-graph edge, and measures the resulting drop in detection accuracy; the specific critique that the constraint "the adversary cannot alter the honest graph" assumed by most Sybil-detection accuracy claims does not bound this attack.

targets.title: Sybil Detection Using Graph Neural Networks
targets.authors: Stuart Heeb, Andreas Plesner, Roger Wattenhofer
targets.why_needed: SYBILGAT: applies a graph attention network that assigns learned, per-neighbor attention weights during aggregation rather than the fixed propagation weights of SybilRank/SybilBelief, evaluated on a real Twitter graph exceeding 269,000 nodes and 6.8 million edges; states a specific claim of improved robustness against a large count of attack edges, the exact failure mode of the earlier propagation-based methods, so its measured attack-edge-count-versus-accuracy curve is the number to extract.

targets.title: More Efficient Sybil Detection Mechanisms Leveraging Resistance of Users to Attack Requests
targets.authors: Ali Safarpoor-Dehkordi, Ahad N. Zehmakan
targets.why_needed: Models honest users as probabilistically resistant to accepting an attack edge (rather than accepting attack requests at a fixed rate) and states a detection mechanism whose message/computation cost is measurably lower than prior random-walk mechanisms at the same accuracy, under that resistance model; a 2025 result to check against the 2013 SoK's stated gap for a targeted-attachment adversary.

targets.title: Graph-Based Fake Account Detection: A Survey
targets.authors: Ali Safarpoor-Dehkordi, Ahad N. Zehmakan
targets.why_needed: A 2025 survey specifically of graph-based (including GNN-based) fake-account and Sybil detection, positioned to state which post-2013 methods it classifies as still reducible to the local-community-detection pattern Alvisi (S&P 2013) critiqued and which it considers structurally different; the freshest available systematization of this specific sub-literature.

targets.title: SyRA: Sybil-Resilient Anonymous Signatures with Applications to Decentralized Identity
targets.authors: Elizabeth C. Crites, Aggelos Kiayias, Markulf Kohlweiss, Amirreza Sarencheh
targets.why_needed: A cryptographic (not graph-based) approach to Sybil resistance: each user holds one credential from an issuer and can derive unlinkable pseudonyms per context, with a signature proving pseudonym-credential consistency in zero-knowledge, so admission depends on possessing one credential rather than on graph position or a pre-trusted seed set. Directly answers the domain brief's request for a construction claiming forgery resistance without a trusted seed identity; the specific thing to check on full read is whether the credential issuer itself is a new trusted party the construction has simply relocated rather than removed. The 2024 IACR ePrint version (2024/379) predates the CCS 2025 publication.

targets.title: De-SyRIS: A Decentralized Sybil-Resistant Identity System without a Trusted Credential Issuer
targets.authors: Michal Ľaš, Ivan Homoliak, Juraj Mariani
targets.why_needed: States it is the first Sybil-resistant identity system that is fully decentralized without any centralized credential issuer, combining facial-biometric verification, anti-Sybil social-graph analysis, zero-knowledge proofs, and trusted execution environments; directly targets the exact unsolved problem the domain brief states ("Sybil resistance without trusted seeds") and CRITES-CCS-25's unresolved issuer-relocation question, so the specific thing to extract on full read is which of the four named mechanisms is doing the actual trust-anchoring work and whether the trusted-execution-environment manufacturer becomes a new trusted party.

targets.title: MeritRank: Sybil Tolerant Reputation for Merit-Based Tokenomics
targets.authors: Bulat Nasrulin, Georgy Ishmaev, Johan Pouwelse
targets.why_needed: Combines a decayed, feedback-weighted random-walk reputation score (subjective per-viewer, no global aggregation) with an explicit Sybil-tolerance proof bounding the reputation gain obtainable per unit of resource an attacker controls, positioned as a merit-based alternative to token-stake reputation; the closest target in this domain to a reputation construction that states a formal Sybil-resistance bound without relying on a trusted seed set, so its assumptions and proof structure are the specific things to check on full read.
